newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish helicopters strike at Kurd guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Turkish helicopters strike at Kurd guerrillas.

text.p: Turkish army helicopters fired rockets at rebel positions on Thursday in an air offensive against Kurdish guerrillas in the eastern mountains, security officials said.
They said two U.S.-made Cobra helicopters attacked Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) fighters in the province of Tunceli. No details of casualties were immediately available.
Air force jets bombed Alibogazi, an almost inaccessible ravine in Tunceli used as a rebel hideout, on Tuesday and Wednesday, the officials said.

Fighting in the province's rugged countryside often increases in March when winter snow begins to melt. The rebels abducted a civilian at a roadblock on a main artery through the mountains earlier this week, the officials said.
More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old Kurdish conflict in southeast Turkey and northern Iraq.
A court has charged an Islamist mayor from Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party with aiding the rebels, judicial officials said.
Behrun Aygoren, mayor of the southeastern town of Dicle, was arrested on Wednesday and charged at a night session of the state security court in the city of Diyarbakir, they said.
Aygoren was elected as an independent at local polls in 1994 but later joined Welfare.
